reviewBoundary: Four original junior fifteen-gap four-choice narratives. Fictional travel, theatre, mural and sports incidents. Same-author context, all-key and alternative review, shuffled options. No independent calibration claimed.

units.title: A drawing at the station
units.alignmentNote: One complete original fifteen-gap four-choice passage. Source is a level/family reference, not copied language or a claim of exact source-paper difficulty.

materials.title: A drawing at the station
materials.text:
At a station in another country, my family could not find the platform for our train. Dad showed the ____1____ to a member of staff, but the place name sounded different when she said it. We were not sure we had understood.

I had a notebook in my bag. I drew three little platforms and a bridge. The woman smiled and took my ____2____. She crossed out the first platform, circled the third and drew an arrow over the bridge.

"Third platform?" Dad asked, holding up three ____3____. She nodded. Then she pointed to the clock. We still had twenty minutes, so we did not need to ____4____.

Mum had a heavy case. We found a lift beside them. A sign showed that it went to the ____5____. From there, we could cross and go down on the other side.

On the platform, the board showed our train number. We checked it against the ticket instead of trusting the ____6____ alone. Another train was going to a place with a similar name.

When our train arrived, we thanked the woman again as she walked past. She gave my notebook a thumbs-up. My quick drawing had not been ____7____, but it had done its job.

On the train, my sister added drawings of our cases. We kept the page as a ____8____ of the trip.

Before travelling, I had worried about not knowing enough ____9____. I still wanted to learn more, but I had discovered another way to ____10____. A simple picture could support a question, not replace every ____11____. We still checked signs and numbers. And when we were unsure, we asked ____12____ instead of pretending to understand. That small pause made the journey feel ____13____, not slower. I kept the notebook ____14____ for the rest of the holiday, ready for the next conversation that needed more than ____15____.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: A train ticket contains the destination and number they need to check. Breakfast, newspaper and a generic photo do not supply those booking details.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: She uses the pencil to alter the drawing. Clothing, luggage and footwear cannot draw the described marks.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: Holding up three fingers checks the number. Three bags, tickets or clocks would not be this hand gesture.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: Twenty minutes means there is no need to rush. Waiting and listening remain useful, while drawing is already helping.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: The lift reaches the bridge so they can cross over and descend. The route is not to a shop, street or directly into a train.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: A similar place name makes number checking necessary. Colour, price and weather are not the confusing destination information.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: The rough functional drawing need not be beautiful. Weight, sound and wetness do not express its artistic quality.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: The illustrated page preserves a memory of the journey. It is not a danger notice, payment demand or rule.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: Language uncertainty concerns not knowing enough words. Games, songs and recipes do not address their communication problem.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: The drawing helps communicate with staff. Competition, sleeping and cooking are not the station interaction.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 11.
questions.explanation: A picture supports an explanation but does not replace all verbal clarification. It is not a substitute for a physical window, bridge or case.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 12.
questions.explanation: When unsure, they ask again for clarification. Yesterday, outside and alone do not indicate repeating a question.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 13.
questions.explanation: Checking information makes the journey safer from mistakes. It does not change temperature, noise or physical route length.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 14.
questions.explanation: Keeping the notebook handy makes it available for another conversation. Closed, empty and secret do not emphasise readiness.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.
questions.explanation: The story contrasts words with visual support. Money, clothes and food do not name the original communication medium.

units.title: A line from the chorus
units.alignmentNote: One complete original fifteen-gap four-choice passage. Source is a level/family reference, not copied language or a claim of exact source-paper difficulty.

materials.title: A line from the chorus
materials.text:
I had only two lines in our school play, but I practised them every evening. Theo had the main part. I thought his job was much more ____1____ than mine.

During the final rehearsal, Theo stopped in the middle of a speech. He looked at the teacher. He had forgotten the next ____2____. Before the teacher could speak, several of us in the chorus said it quietly together. Theo continued.

Afterwards, he thanked us. I was surprised. I had learned his speech simply because I heard it so ____3____. 

On performance night, a piece of scenery fell sideways behind us. Nobody was hurt, but it covered the door through which I was supposed to ____4____. For a second I could think only about my two perfect lines.

Then I remembered Theo's pause. I looked at the other actors instead of the closed door. One moved aside, leaving a clear ____5____ at the other end of the stage. I walked across, said my lines and joined the chorus.

The audience did not seem to notice the change. Our teacher later said we had kept the story moving. Instead of following every step exactly, we had ____6____ one another.

While putting away our costumes, Theo asked whether I would join the next play. "You were very ____7____ when the door disappeared," he said. I laughed. I had not felt calm inside.

 I no longer counted a role's ____8____ only by the number of words. Listening was also part of the ____9____. Knowing the whole scene helped me react when something went ____10____. A good performance was not a row of people waiting for their own ____11____. It was a group paying attention ____12____. Next rehearsal, I brought my script and gave the whole scene my ____13____. I practised my lines, but I also watched where everyone moved. A small part could make a ____14____ if its actor stayed involved from beginning to ____15____.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: The narrator initially equates the main role with importance. Comfort, colour and price do not describe this status comparison.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: Theo forgets the next spoken line, which the chorus supplies. Clothing, an exit and a ticket cannot complete his speech.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: Repeated rehearsals explain learning the speech. Quietness, lateness and location do not explain familiarity as directly.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: The planned door is the exit through which the narrator should leave. Sleeping, painting and eating are not the stage movement.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: An actor moves aside to provide clear space for an alternative exit. The other nouns do not name a passage across the stage.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: The chorus supplies a forgotten line and another actor clears a route: mutual help. Blame, copying and forgetting do not describe that cooperation.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: Theo praises outward calm, explicitly contrasted with feeling uncalm inside. Anger, carelessness and absence do not fit.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: The narrator changes how a role’s value is judged. Length is the old measure itself, while colour and price are unrelated.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: Listening is part of the actor’s job. It is not clothing, the watching crowd or itself a problem.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: Unexpected forgotten lines and scenery trouble mean something goes wrong. Well reverses this, and home/upstairs are locations.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 11.
questions.explanation: Actors waiting only for their own turn neglect the whole scene. Meal, bus and holiday are not the performance sequence.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 12.
questions.explanation: The lesson is shared attention together. Yesterday is time, instead lacks the right contrast and alone reverses teamwork.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 13.
questions.explanation: Bringing attention figuratively means listening and watching the entire scene. Food, admission ticket and umbrella do not supply that engagement.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 14.
questions.explanation: Make a difference means contribute meaningfully, the story’s point. Noise and mistakes are not the desired contribution; no new promise is being made.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.
questions.explanation: From beginning to end expresses involvement throughout. Door, night and word do not complete this temporal pair.

units.title: The wall with an extra shape

materials.title: The wall with an extra shape
materials.text:
Our class designed a mural for the youth centre. Each person painted one section, and I was responsible for a large round yellow sun. I wanted it to be a perfect ____1____.

While I reached for another brush, my sleeve touched the wet paint. A yellow mark spread beyond the line. I tried to ____2____ it, but the colour had already soaked into the rough wall.

The teacher asked me to step back. From close up, the mark seemed enormous. From across the room, it was only one small part of a much ____3____ picture.

Hana suggested making it a ray of sunlight. I objected that the design showed no rays. She asked whether the design was a plan or a ____4____ that nobody could change.

We discussed it with the group. The extra shape would not cover anyone else's painting. We agreed to add similar shapes around the sun. The first mark no longer looked ____5____.

When the centre opened, a visitor asked who had thought of the lively sunlight. I nearly said it had been my idea. Then I explained about my sleeve and Hana's suggestion. The visitor laughed ____6____, not at me. She liked the account.

I had expected to feel ____7____ every time I saw the wall. Instead, it reminded me of our conversation. It had given the group a chance to make the work ____8____.

That did not mean mistakes always improved things. If the paint had covered another person's section, we would have needed a different ____9____. We had considered the whole picture and the people ____10____. I stopped treating a plan as too ____11____ to discuss. A shared project needed room for ____12____ as well as preparation. The yellow mark had not ruined our work. With everyone's ____13____, it had become part of it. For our final photograph, Hana and I pointed to the ray. I felt ____14____ to tell its ____15____.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: A sun with a carefully drawn round edge is a circle. Square, triangle and line do not match the intended outline.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: The unwanted spread is to be removed, but soaked-in colour resists. Collecting, measuring and framing do not undo it.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: The mural as a whole is larger than the one close-up mark. Smaller reverses scale, and colour/age are not the perspective contrast.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: Hana challenges whether the design is an unchangeable rule. Story, picture and question do not imply a prohibition on change.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: Repeating similar rays makes the original mark look intentional rather than accidental. It remains bright, yellow and visible.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: The visitor laughs warmly, expressly not mocking the narrator. Anger, secrecy and nervousness are unsupported.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: The narrator initially expects embarrassment at the mistake. Hunger, sleepiness and boredom do not relate to the flawed paint.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: The group improves the shared design by incorporating rays. Disappearance, reduced scale and privacy are not the result.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: Covering someone else’s work would demand a different solution. Changing visitor, clothing or photograph would not repair that harm.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: The relevant people are those involved in the shared project. Being outside, asleep or absent does not establish their stake.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 11.
questions.explanation: Treating a plan as fixed prevents discussing changes. Simplicity, colour and size do not express immutability.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 12.
questions.explanation: The story balances preparation with room for change. Silence, blame and secrecy would block the shared discussion.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 13.
questions.explanation: The group explicitly agrees after checking effects on others. Surprise, fear and absence do not supply shared permission.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 14.
questions.explanation: The final pride and photograph show being happy to tell the story. Fear, inability and regret oppose that change.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.
questions.explanation: Tell its story means explain how the ray came about. Price, future and colour do not name that account.

units.title: The whistle instead of the gloves

materials.title: The whistle instead of the gloves
materials.text:
After training all term as goalkeeper, I hurt my wrist before the school tournament. The doctor said I could watch but must not play. I put my gloves in my bag, feeling that my whole ____1____ had been wasted.

Our teacher asked whether I would help with the younger pupils' match. They needed someone to keep time and signal when play should ____2____. I did not want the job. Watching seemed a poor substitute.

Still, I agreed. The teacher explained this short practice game. She would supervise and make any difficult ____3____. I would whistle at agreed times and explain the signals.

One child stood apart. Whenever the ball came near, two stronger players took it. She had hardly had a ____4____.

At a break, the teacher asked how to include everyone. I wanted to tell them the answer, but she let them ____5____ it. They agreed to pass to different teammates before trying to score.

Play became slower, with missed passes, but more children became ____6____. The quiet player finally received the ball and sent it towards a teammate. She smiled.

When the match ended, she asked if I would help next week.  I still wanted to ____7____, and I would when it was safe. But I had not spent the afternoon doing nothing.

From the goal, I usually judged a match by how many shots I ____8____. From the side, I could see another kind of success: people learning to play ____9____. My role had clear ____10____, rather than requiring expert refereeing. Taking it seriously had helped me stay part of the ____11____. I went home less ____12____ than I had arrived. My place in football did not depend entirely ____13____ my gloves. There were other ways to ____14____ while waiting to return to my usual ____15____.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: Training all term is the effort the narrator fears was wasted. Holiday, lunch and admission are not the investment described.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: The timekeeper signals when play stops. Growth, sleep and travel are not the match signal.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: A supervising teacher makes difficult rule decisions. Decoration, journeys and promises are not adjudication.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: The excluded child rarely receives a turn with the ball. A coat, lesson or whistle does not express participation.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: The teacher allows teams to discuss how to include everyone. Hiding, forgetting and selling do not produce their agreed passing rule.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: More passing opportunities involve more children. Absence and silence do not express participation; confusion is not the stated improvement.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: The goalkeeper still wants to play when safe. Leaving, teaching and complaining are not the return blocked by the wrist injury.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: A goalkeeper judges performance by shots saved. Took would be an attacking role, heard is unrelated and counted measures quantity without keeping goals out.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: The improvement is inclusive teamwork, playing together. Yesterday is time, outside location and alone the opposite of the lesson.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: The teacher handles difficult decisions and defines a limited supporting role. Prizes, secrets and colours do not express those boundaries.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 11.
questions.explanation: Helping with the match keeps the narrator part of the game. Problem, audience and injury do not name meaningful football participation.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 12.
questions.explanation: The initial frustration decreases after a useful role. Thirst, sleepiness and hunger are not the emotional change.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 13.
questions.explanation: Depend on is the required construction. From, with and at do not complete depend here.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 14.
questions.explanation: Helping others is a contribution while unable to compete. Recover names healing rather than a football role, and disappear reverses involvement.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.
questions.explanation: The usual goalkeeper position is the intended return. Classroom, doctor and holiday are not that football role.
